files.text:
Return every brass key before closing.

Never leave the blue cabinet unlocked.

For example, the small box holds spare keys.

Record each delivery beside its receipt.

Never discard a receipt before review.

For example, the parcel arrives on Tuesday.

Count the green trays at the end of service.

Never stack a cracked tray above the counter.

For example, six trays fit on one shelf.

        atom: { kind: instruction, polarity: obligation }
      - name: prohibition
        description: A unit that tells the reader what never to do.
        atom: { kind: instruction, polarity: prohibition }
      - name: example
        description: A unit that shows a case and is not itself an instruction.

body.system: You label numbered units of a document. For each unit give exactly one label from the list, or none. Answer with JSON only, no other text: {"labels": [{"units": "<n> or <a>-<b>", "label": "<name>"}]}. An entry with a label other than none also gives "anchor": the first three words of the first unit it names, copied from its start, so code can check the entry is on the unit you mean. Every unit must appear once. Units labelled none still appear, joined in ranges, with no anchor. A range joins neighbouring units that share a label, and may cross a line marked not labelable: only the units in it take the label. A line marked not labelable takes no label, not even none: leave its number out of the answer. For a label that asks for a target, add "target": the number of the unit that holds the other end. A target must be a unit that can be labelled, never a line marked not labelable. Never copy text from the units, except an anchor and the words of a span.
